text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA

- The leu's reference rate against the dollar depreciated by 2.3 percent over Nov 25-Dec 1. The currency trades at around 5,000 to the dollar at retail currency shops, against an interbank market price of some 3,600. The difference between the two rates is expected to widen by Christmas.
ADEVARUL
- Chemical plant Oltchim SA won a bourse quotation, becoming the 17th stock listed on the Bucharest exchange.
TINERETUL LIBER
- The State Ownership Fund managed to privatise 1,122 state companies so far this year.
- The first nuclear reactor of the Cernavoda power plant is contributing 720 megawatts to the national grid.
AZI
- A canned fruit and vegetables factory in Tulcea struck a joint venture deal with the Italian company Megafin. The Romanian partner will invest $23 million in upgrading over the next 12 months.
ZIUA
- A court ruling on the fate of the troubled Banca Dacia Felix SA is to be issued only after a new cabinet has been formed, judge Ioan Georgiu said.
- Radu Vasile, secretary-general of the National Peasant Party said Romania needed external financing worth $1.5 billion in 1997.
CRONICA ROMANA
- The Communications Ministry awarded a GSM licence to the Mobifon consortium, which paid a licence fee of $50 million.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- German company Moksel, which holds 51 percent of Agricola International farming company, plans to sell off its stake over disappointment with company activities.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The newspaper comments on Sunday's presidential run-off in neighbouring Moldova, which placed Petru Lucinschi ahead of Mircea Snegur.
- It prints a list of possible ministers in the new government. It also presents the five leftist parties in Romania, of which three are represented to parliament.
ADEVARUL
- The prospects of Romanian-U.S. relations have never been better, said U.S. vice-president Al Gore after meeting President Emil Constantinescu at the OSCE summit in Lisbon.
- Outgoing Foreign Minister Teodor Melescanu will head the foreign policy commission in the upper house, the Senate.
- The newspaper publishes a report on Constantinescu's private meetings with heads of state and prime ministers at the OSCE summit.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Bucharest's two infectious disease hospitals confirmed 20 cases of viral hepatitis in five days.
- Constantinescu and his Ukrainean counterpart agreed to reopen negotiations on a bilateral treaty between Romania and Ukraine.
- The newspaper publishes excerpts from the governing programme to be presented before parliament later this week.
LIBERTATEA
- Moldova elected a politician close to Moscov as President, the newspaper says on Petru Lucinschi's victory.

- Parliament's two houses must first create their commissions which should hear all candidates for the new cabinet before they are presented in a joint parliamentary session by Prime Minister designate Victor Ciorbea.
CRONICA ROMANA
- The Party of Social Democracy must be a party of the interests of the many, says outgoing President Ion Iliescu, now leader of the party. ($=3,611 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
